answers.answer: Shuffle all four Conflict III cards and place all four face down at the bottom; shuffle the nine II cards and deal five face down above them; shuffle the three I cards and deal one face down on top. Return unused I and II cards to the box without looking at them.
answers.evidence: Setup: “face-down 10-card Conflict Deck” with 1 I, 5 II, 4 III; return unused cards unseen.

answers.answer: In four-player play, each human starts at 1 VP; in three-player play, at 0 VP. Each starts with two Agents on the Leader and a third (Swordmaster) beside the board; three troops in their garrison and nine in supply; and 1 water.
answers.evidence: Setup 6: Score marker on 1 in a 4-player game, otherwise 0; two Agents on Leader; third Agent Swordmaster; three cubes in garrison, nine troops in supply; take 1 water.

answers.answer: Yes, you may take a Reveal turn while Agents remain, and after Revealing your turns are skipped for the rest of that phase, so you cannot later take an Agent turn that round. Reveal effects come only from the Reveal boxes of cards revealed from the remaining hand, not cards used on Agent turns. At Clean Up, move all cards in front of you from both types of turns to your discard pile.
answers.evidence: Player Turns: “you may take a Reveal turn while you still have Agents”; after Reveal, turns skipped. Reveal effects apply to just-revealed cards; Clean Up moves all cards in front of you to discard.

answers.answer: Before placing the Agent, you may play a legal Plot Intrigue on your own Agent turn; resources it grants before entry can pay that entry cost. Effects from the Agent card being played or from the destination occur after placement and cannot pay for that same entry. One card lets you choose only one Agent icon and send one Agent. A card with no Agent icons cannot be played on an Agent turn; it can only be revealed.
answers.evidence: Player Turns: entry paid before placement/effects; pre-placement Plot resource gains can pay. Agent Turn: “one card can't send multiple Agents”; no-icon cards only revealed.

answers.answer: At a Combat space, deploy all three troops recruited that turn plus up to two of the four troops already in your garrison, for at most five. At a non-Combat space, you cannot deploy troops there; they go into the garrison when recruited. Troops are recruited from your supply into the garrison. (The question’s non-Combat contrast concerns the deployment allowance; there is no deployment at a non-Combat space.)
answers.evidence: Recruiting & Deploying: cube recruits from supply into garrison; Combat-space turn deploys any/all units recruited that turn plus up to two more from garrison.

answers.answer: A Spy Agent icon on a card lets you send an Agent to any space connected to an observation post where you currently have a Spy; you do not recall that Spy. Infiltrate recalls your Spy from a connected post to enter a space occupied by another player, ignoring that Agent; it cannot bypass your own Agent. Gather Intelligence recalls a Spy from a connected post to draw a card, chosen immediately after placing your Agent and before receiving space or played-card effects. You may not use the same Spy for both, but may recall two different Spies for Infiltrate and Gather Intelligence on one placement.
answers.evidence: Special Rules — Spies: Spy Agent icon does not recall; Infiltrate bypasses another player's Agent only; Gather timing after placement; same Spy cannot do both.

answers.answer: Two troops give 4 strength, one sandworm 3 and four revealed swords 4, totaling 11. If your final unit is removed, your strength becomes 0. With no unit in the Conflict you cannot play Combat Intrigue, since it requires at least one deployed unit.
answers.evidence: Strength: troop 2, sandworm 3, sword 1; if last unit removed strength is 0. Intrigue cards: Combat only during Combat and only with at least one unit deployed.

answers.answer: Yes. Passing does not prevent you from acting again; the window closes after all involved players pass consecutively. After rewards, return troops from the Conflict to their supply (not garrison), reset all Combat markers to 0, and return sandworms to the bank.
answers.evidence: Combat Intrigue: “not required to pass just because you passed earlier”; resolve after consecutive passes. Cleanup returns troops to supply, resets markers, returns worms to bank.

answers.answer: With exactly two tied for first in a four-player game, each tied player receives the second reward; the remaining players compete for the third reward, and nobody wins or takes the Conflict card. With the same tie in a three-player game, each tied player receives the second reward and there are no other rewards; nobody takes the card. A player with 0 strength receives no reward.
answers.evidence: Combat ties table: exactly two tied first with four players leaves remaining players competing for third; with 3 or fewer no other rewards; nobody takes card. Resolve Combat: 0 strength receives none.

answers.answer: Having one or more sandworms doubles the rewards once; two sandworms do not quadruple them. Taking control of a location and battle icons on Conflict cards cannot be doubled. For an optional 3-spice-for-1-VP reward, you may pay 3 spice once for 1 VP, or pay the cost a second time (6 total) for 2 VP.
answers.evidence: Sandworm Reward Doubling: one or more worms double; control and battle icons excluded; example permits paying 3 spice again for a second VP.

answers.answer: After winning a Conflict and taking its card face up into your supply, check for a matching battle icon on another face-up Conflict or Objective card in your supply. A match is mandatory: flip the pair face down and gain 1 VP. In the Endgame, the wild icon may match any one of the three battle icons in your supply; flip the pair for 1 VP.
answers.evidence: Battle Icons: win and take card, check another face-up Conflict or Objective; “must” flip matching pair; Endgame wild may match any of three.

answers.answer: At 2 Influence, gain 1 VP; falling below 2 loses it, and reaching 2 again regains it. At 4, gain the printed track bonus, which is retained after falling below 4 and earned again on returning to 4; the first player to 4 also gets the Alliance token and its 1 VP, which remains only while holding the token. Tying the holder at 4 does not transfer it: a challenger must rise above the holder. The FAQ also says if the holder loses Influence after having been tied, the formerly tied opponent takes it (or, if several were tied, the former holder chooses); if nobody has 4+ when holder falls to 3 or less, return the token to the board.
answers.evidence: Faction Influence: separate reversal rules for track bonus and Alliance VP; tying does not steal; FAQ transfer triggers described.

answers.answer: During your Reveal turn, Persuasion may be spent before, between or after Reveal effects. Pool Persuasion from different sources to buy one card or split one source across cards; unused Persuasion is lost. You may buy from any of the five Imperium Row cards or either Reserve stack, at the cost printed at the card’s top right. After buying a Row card, replace it from the Imperium Deck and you may buy the replacement if affordable. Acquired cards go face up into your discard pile and are not used immediately.
answers.evidence: Acquiring Cards: Reveal-turn spending windows, pooling/splitting, cost location, immediate Row replacement, discard destination.

answers.answer: At the Makers phase, add 1 spice to each unoccupied Maker space’s bonus spot; accumulated bonus spice remains until an Agent visits, and the visitor gains all of it, including when choosing worms. Deep Desert costs 3 water and offers 4 base spice or, with Maker Hooks, two worms; Hagga Basin costs 1 water and offers 2 base spice or, with Hooks, one worm. Hooks are required only when the summoning effect specifies them and are retained, not spent. While the Shield Wall remains, worms cannot be summoned to Arrakeen, Spice Refinery or Imperial Basin; removing the Wall allows summoning to any Conflict. A sandworm is placed directly in your Conflict quadrant and never in a garrison.
answers.evidence: Makers; Sandworms; Maker Reward Doubling sections; Deep Desert/Hagga table: bonus spice gained on visit; Wall protects three locations; worms never in garrison.

answers.answer: At Recall, if any player is at 10+ VP or the Conflict Deck is empty, Endgame is triggered. Players first may play and resolve any Endgame Intrigue cards, then compare total VP. The listed tie-breakers in order are spice, Solari, water, then garrisoned troops.
answers.evidence: Phase 5 Recall and Scoring: end trigger checked at end of round; Endgame Intrigue before winner; tiebreak order.

answers.answer: Standard CHOAM setup shuffles all 20 standard contracts face down, then exposes two face up and leaves 18 face down in the bank. Shuffle the four added Intrigue cards into the Intrigue Deck and four added Imperium cards into the Imperium Deck. Shaddam is optional. The ten contrasting-back Rise of Ix contracts are left in the box and are not part of this standard setup.
answers.evidence: CHOAM setup changes: without Shaddam, shuffle all 20, two offers, 18 bank; add four cards of each type. Scope/components exclude contrasting-back set.

answers.answer: With CHOAM and contracts available, the icon lets you take one face-up contract and replace it with a face-up one from the bank. If all contracts have been taken by players, the icon instead gives 2 Solari. A Harvest contract is completed by sending an Agent to a Maker space and gaining the printed spice amount that turn in total, including other sources; an Immediate contract completes as soon as taken; Acquire The Spice Must Flow completes when you next acquire that card.
answers.evidence: Taking contracts and Completing contracts sections specify icon behavior and each contract completion condition.

answers.answer: No. If you take a contract for a space after already sending your Agent there that turn, you must wait until a future turn; you must hold the contract when sending the Agent. When completing it, announce it, gain its listed rewards, then flip it face down and leave it in your supply.
answers.evidence: Completing contracts: if Agent already sent this turn, wait until future turn; announce, gain rewards, flip face down and leave in supply.

answers.answer: Use one shared scoring Rival. It receives the Ornithopter Objective; the humans randomly receive the other two eligible Objectives, and the human whose card shows the First Player marker goes first. Turn order is First Player → Rival → other human; First Player alternates only between the humans. The Rival never takes a Reveal turn. Its 10+ VP can trigger Endgame at Recall, and it can win by having the most VP.
answers.evidence: Required Rival Rules setup and Agent turns; Rival can win and its 10+ VP triggers Endgame like a human.

answers.answer: For an occupied destination, ignore it and reveal another Hagal card. A Place Spy card does not place an Agent: try an empty post of the specified type; if none exists, ignore placement, then immediately reveal another Hagal card and continue the same Agent turn. Ignore ordinary board-space costs and effects; apply only Hagal effects. If House Hagal empties or Reshuffle appears, immediately reshuffle it and continue.
answers.evidence: Rival Agent turns: ignore occupied destination and reveal again; Place Spy behavior; ignore normal costs/effects; empty/Reshuffle instruction.

answers.answer: For standard three- or four-player setup, remove Objective cards marked for a different player count, shuffle the eligible cards and deal one face up to each player; whoever has the Objective showing the First Player marker takes it. Shaddam may be chosen only when playing with the CHOAM Module.
answers.evidence: Setup 3 says do not use Shaddam unless CHOAM; Setup 5 says omit mismatched Objective cards, shuffle and distribute face up; marked card determines first player.

answers.answer: Solari, spice, water and sandworms are not meant to be limited; make any convenient substitution if the bank runs out. If your personal troop supply runs out, you cannot recruit more until troops return there. When gaining resources take them from the bank, and when paying return them to the bank; the summary does not allow taking tokens from another player's supply.
answers.evidence: Setup 7: resources/sandworms not limited; gains from bank and payments return there. Recruiting: no troop supply means cannot recruit more.

answers.answer: The five phases are Round Start, Player Turns, Combat, Makers, Recall. At Round Start first reveal a Conflict from the top of the deck and resolve any defensive troop bonus; then each player draws five cards from their deck. At Recall, if Endgame is not triggered, recall Agents to Leaders, pass First Player clockwise and start the next round.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure lists five phases and order; Phase 1 conflict reveal then defensive bonus then draw five; Phase 5 next-round procedure.

answers.answer: Yes. After paying entry and placing the Agent, gain board-space effects and Agent-box effects, and advance Influence for a Faction space; these effects may be carried out in any order. You cannot use that visit's Influence to meet its entry requirement because costs and requirements must be met before resolving effects.
answers.evidence: Agent Turn: pay costs/requirements before placement; then effects and Faction advance may be done in any order.

answers.answer: No. An arrow cost/effect may be used only once per turn; sandworm doubling of a Conflict-card reward is the stated exception. Most card and space effects are mandatory, with exceptions for “may,” optional arrow costs, and optional black-X trash. Intrigue conditions and costs must be met to play it.
answers.evidence: Arrows: pay and gain only once per turn except sandworm reward doubling. FAQ: mandatory effects and costs exceptions; Intrigue conditions/costs required.

answers.answer: Place a Spy from your supply on an unoccupied observation post; if no Spy is in supply, you may first recall one of your Spies for no effect. If an effect specifies a particular Agent-icon type connected to the post, the post must connect to that icon or placement is not allowed.
answers.evidence: Special Rules — Spies: placement at unoccupied post; may recall from post if supply empty; specified Agent icon must connect.

answers.answer: No: Infiltrate bypasses only another player's Agent, not your own. A Spy cannot be recalled to use Infiltrate or Gather Intelligence without still playing a card for the Agent turn. You may not recall two Spies for Gather Intelligence on the same placement; you may recall one for Gather Intelligence and another for Infiltrate.
answers.evidence: Spies section: Infiltrate cannot bypass own Agent; FAQ says recalling Spy requires playing an Agent card; two different effects allowed, never two Gather Intelligence.

answers.answer: The controller receives the location bonus whenever any player, including the controller, visits: 1 Solari at Arrakeen or Spice Refinery, 1 spice at Imperial Basin. Winning the corresponding Conflict gives control by placing your marker on the flag, replacing an opponent's marker. When that Conflict is revealed while you already control the location, you may deploy one troop from your supply to the Conflict without visiting it.
answers.evidence: Critical Locations & Control: visit bonus, control transfer on win, defensive troop from supply on reveal.

answers.answer: If two tie for second in a three-player Conflict, each tied player gets the third reward; the first-place winner retains the first reward and card, and no further rewards are given. Players tied for third get nothing. If three players tie for first, each gets the second reward, nobody takes the card, and there are no other rewards in either three- or four-player games.
answers.evidence: Combat ties: tie for second gets third reward; tie for third nothing. Three tied for first section says each gets second; no other rewards.

answers.answer: In an ordinary three-player Conflict with three different positive strengths, first and second place receive the first and second rewards; third receives nothing. This is also the rule for a two-human game with its Rival as the third participant; ordinary third place gets nothing unless tied for second.
answers.evidence: Resolve Combat: for 2 or 3 players, ordinary first and second receive rewards, third nothing; includes two humans plus a Rival.

answers.answer: Plot Intrigues may be played during your own Agent or Reveal turn; Combat Intrigues during Combat only if you have at least one unit in the Conflict; Endgame Intrigues at game end. Keep Intrigues face down separately from your deck and reveal only when played; after resolving, put them face up in a discard pile next to their deck. If the Intrigue Deck runs out, shuffle its discard pile to form a new deck.
answers.evidence: Intrigue cards section and FAQ: types/timing, storage/discard, reshuffle exhausted deck.

answers.answer: An ordinary discard instruction cannot discard an Intrigue unless it says so; discard a card of your choice from your hand, not from in play or your discard pile. Secrets' Steal Intrigue effect takes one Intrigue selected at random from each opponent who has at least four Intrigues.
answers.evidence: Discarding: from hand and not Intrigue unless specified. Secrets: each opponent with 4+ gives one selected at random.

answers.answer: A trash effect may remove cards from your hand, discard pile or in play. Return ordinary trashed cards to the box; Reserve cards return to their Reserve stack. Trashing is optional unless it is a cost or a card directs you to trash itself. The Spice Must Flow's acquire VP is retained even if the card is later trashed.
answers.evidence: Trashing section covers eligible places and destinations/optionality; FAQ Victory says acquire VP retained if trashed.

answers.answer: An acquire-box effect resolves once at the moment the card is acquired. When unable to draw because your deck is empty, shuffle your discard pile into a new deck and continue. Unused Persuasion cannot be saved; it is lost at the end of your Reveal turn.
answers.evidence: Acquire box; Acquiring Cards says reshuffle when deck empty and Persuasion never saved.

answers.answer: Cards played on Agent turns and cards revealed on the Reveal turn stay face up and in play until Clean Up. Fremen Bond works when you have one or more other Fremen cards in play; two Bond cards may activate each other regardless of which was played first. They cease being in play at Clean Up unless trashed earlier.
answers.evidence: In play / Fremen Bond: other Fremen cards count; two Bond cards activate one another regardless of order; remain until Clean Up.

answers.answer: Recall Agent returns one of your other Agents on the board, not the Agent sent this turn; the returned Agent may be used on a later Agent turn in the same round. A retreated troop moves from the Conflict to your garrison. “Retreat any number” includes zero.
answers.evidence: Recall Agent icon and Retreat definitions; FAQ Combat says retreat any number allows zero.

answers.answer: No. A free-choice effect gaining two Influence means choose one Faction and gain both there, not split between two Factions. An Alliance icon requires holding that Faction's Alliance token; a minimum-Influence effect requires meeting its stated Influence threshold.
answers.evidence: Influence special rule: gain two with free choice cannot choose two different Factions; Alliance and minimum Influence requirements.

answers.answer: If the holder loses Influence after being tied by two opponents, the formerly tied opponent takes the Alliance; if several were tied, the former holder chooses which receives it. If the holder falls to 3 or lower and nobody has 4+, return the token to the board and the former holder loses its VP.
answers.evidence: Official FAQ — Alliance loss details both formerly tied recipient and return-to-board condition.

answers.answer: A card drawn during Reveal is immediately revealed and used that turn. A card drawn after Reveal stays for next round, when you draw five additional cards. A Plot Intrigue played earlier with an effect that applies at Reveal stays face up until then, is used, then discarded.
answers.evidence: FAQ Draw timing: during Reveal immediate; after Reveal next round plus five; delayed Plot stays face up, then used and discarded.

answers.answer: No. A “when you win a Conflict” Intrigue cannot be played after a tie for first, since nobody wins. If you receive that Intrigue as a reward for an outright win, it may be played immediately.
answers.evidence: FAQ Combat and troops: cannot play after tying for first; if received as winning reward, can play immediately.

answers.answer: If all four resource tiebreakers remain tied, the player who most recently took a Reveal turn wins. Scores may exceed the printed 12-space track.
answers.evidence: FAQ Victory: all four tiebreakers tied, most recent Reveal wins; scores may exceed printed track's 12.

answers.answer: No. Fulfill all contracts you hold for the same space with one Agent placement; you cannot delay their completion. A board-space contract resolves as another effect of that Agent turn, in any order with the space and Agent-box effects, but you must have held the contract when sending the Agent.
answers.evidence: FAQ Contract completion is mandatory: all same-space contracts with one placement; another effect resolvable in any order; must hold contract at placement.

answers.answer: Shaddam does not start with the set-aside Sardaukar contracts. Before the initial contract shuffle, set aside both; only Shaddam may acquire them, choosing one instead of a generally available contract. His Signet Ring deployment restriction starts immediately when played to send an Agent and applies for that turn, not the rest of the round.
answers.evidence: CHOAM setup and Reserved Sardaukar contracts; FAQ Shaddam says restriction immediately but only that turn.

answers.answer: Feyd's token starts on the leftmost space of his Training track and stays on the rightmost space once it reaches it. Lady Jessica starts with her Lady Jessica side face up, not Reverend Mother Jessica. Reverend Mother Jessica may use her ability on the turn she flips.
answers.evidence: Leader clarifications state Feyd start/end, Jessica starting side, and Reverend Mother ability on flip turn.

answers.answer: Yes. Margot and Irulan count moving from 1 to 3 as reaching 2; reaching 2 with the same Faction can trigger again after losing Influence and later gaining it back. Moving down through 2 does not count as reaching it. Clean Up moving Spacing Guild's Favor from in play to discard does not trigger its discard ability; only discarding it from hand does.
answers.evidence: Leader clarifications: reaching 2 while moving past, can reach again after losing then regaining, not moving down; Guild's Favor triggers only hand discard.

answers.answer: Accept Contract uses the Spice Trade icon, is not a Faction, has no cost and is not a Combat space; it always draws one card, plus gives 2 Solari without CHOAM or when contracts are exhausted, otherwise takes and replaces a face-up contract. It gives no automatic Influence. Dutiful Service uses the Emperor icon, has no cost and is not a Combat space; it gains 1 Emperor Influence (counted once) plus resolves the same contract icon rule. Its Emperor Influence is the automatic Faction advance, counted once.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide identifies icons, status, costs/effects; shared contract rule; faction status clarification says Accept is non-Faction, Dutiful is Emperor and its one Influence counted once.

answers.answer: Arrakeen: City icon, no cost, Combat yes; visitor recruits one troop and draws one card, while its controller separately gains 1 Solari. Fremkit: Fremen icon, no cost, Combat yes; gain 1 Fremen Influence and draw one card. Research Station: City icon, costs 2 water, Combat yes; recruit two troops and draw two cards.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide rows for Arrakeen, Fremkit and Research Station; controller bonus rule.

answers.answer: Deep Desert costs 3 water and offers 4 base spice or, with Hooks, two worms; Hagga Basin costs 1 water and offers 2 base spice or, with Hooks, one worm. Either visit gains all bonus spice at the space even when choosing worms. Hooks are retained, not spent, when summoning.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide rows and Makers section; FAQ Spies says Maker Hooks retained, not spent.

answers.answer: Both Sietch Tabr options require City access and at least 2 Fremen Influence, with no resource entry cost. Option one: take a Maker Hooks token if you lack one, recruit one troop and gain 1 water. Option two: gain 1 water and optionally remove the Shield Wall. The second option gives no troop.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide Sietch Tabr row: two alternatives with shared requirements; troop appears only in first option.

answers.answer: Both High Council visits cost 5 Solari; it is not a Combat space. On the first visit, place your Councilor on an unoccupied seat and gain 2 Persuasion on every Reveal turn for the rest of the game. On later visits, gain 2 spice, draw an Intrigue and recruit three troops.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide High Council row.

answers.answer: Swordmaster costs 8 Solari until anyone obtains one, then costs 6; each player may visit it once per game. Take the third Agent from beside the board onto your Leader, and it is available this round and for the rest of the game. A Rival obtaining its Swordmaster also reduces the human cost to 6.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide Swordmaster row; Rival rules explicitly state Rival obtaining Swordmaster reduces human cost to 6.

answers.answer: Imperial Privilege uses the Landsraad icon, requires at least 2 Emperor Influence, costs 3 Solari and is not a Combat space. You may discard an Intrigue to draw an Intrigue; also recall one of your other Agents and draw a card. It does not automatically grant Emperor Influence.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide Imperial Privilege row; Faction rules distinguish Landsraad from Factions.

answers.answer: Shipping uses Spice Trade access, requires at least 2 Spacing Guild Influence, costs 3 spice, and is not a Combat space. It gives 5 Solari and 1 Influence with any one Faction, which need not be the Guild.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide Shipping row: free-choice Influence; Influence section says icon chooses any one of four Factions.

answers.answer: Gather Support is a non-Combat Landsraad space: choose to pay 0 or 2 Solari; recruit two troops, and if you pay 2 also gain 1 water. Spice Refinery is a Combat City space: choose to pay 0 or 1 spice; gain 2 Solari, or 4 Solari if you paid 1 spice; its controller also gains 1 Solari.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide rows for Gather Support and Spice Refinery.

answers.answer: Heighliner: Spacing Guild, costs 5 spice, gains 1 Guild Influence and recruits five troops; Combat yes. Desert Tactics: Fremen, costs 1 water, gains 1 Fremen Influence, recruits one troop and may trash a card; Combat yes. Sardaukar: Emperor, costs 4 spice, gains 1 Emperor Influence, draws an Intrigue and recruits four troops; Combat no. Deployment is permitted at Heighliner and Desert Tactics, not Sardaukar.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide rows for Heighliner, Desert Tactics and Sardaukar; Combat column.

answers.answer: Assembly Hall uses Landsraad access, has no cost and is not Combat; draw an Intrigue and gain 1 Persuasion during your Reveal turn if your Agent is there. Espionage uses Bene Gesserit access, costs 1 spice, is not Combat; gain 1 Bene Gesserit Influence, draw a card and place a Spy. Deliver Supplies uses Spacing Guild access, no cost, not Combat; gain 1 Guild Influence and 1 water.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide rows for Assembly Hall, Espionage and Deliver Supplies.

answers.answer: Opponents affected by False Orders move their Spy to an empty post not connected to your Agent's destination that turn. It may be played even if no enemy Spy is connected there. Litany Against Fear's red box is ignored during Reveal, or when it gains an Agent icon and is played normally as an Agent card.
answers.evidence: FAQ special clarifications for False Orders and Litany Against Fear.

answers.answer: Opponents cannot acquire a card removed by Manipulate. You may acquire it by other means, but without its 1-Persuasion discount. If it has not been acquired by the end of your next Reveal, remove it from the game.
answers.evidence: FAQ Manipulate ruling.

answers.answer: The Rival starts with four cubes at the bottom of Influence tracks, three troops in its garrison and remaining troops in supply, two Agents in supply plus Swordmaster beside the board, three Spies and 1 water; its score and Combat marker start at 0. Shuffle House Hagal and place it near the Rival, retaining the 2P Reshuffle card. The Rival's 10+ VP triggers Endgame at Recall and it can win.
answers.evidence: Required Rival Setup and Rival can win rule.

answers.answer: As soon as the Rival's total of Solari, spice, Intrigue cards and water reaches its printed Swordmaster value, it spends that value and takes its third Agent for use in the current round. If choosing resources to spend, use Solari, then spice, then Intrigue cards, then water; keep leftovers. The summary does not state a rule for counting differently by resource type; each resource unit counts as one.
answers.evidence: Rival Resources and Swordmaster: count these together, each unit one; spend threshold in stated priority; keep leftovers; Agent usable current round.

answers.answer: Once it has Swordmaster, the Rival spends each set of 7 Solari, 7 spice, 3 Intrigue cards or 3 water for 1 VP. It cannot spend a mixed total of seven resources for a VP; the sets are specific by resource.
answers.evidence: Rival Resources and Swordmaster specifies the four exact sets for 1 VP.

answers.answer: When choosing Influence, the Rival selects the Faction with least Influence, breaking ties by the leftmost priority icon. It gains Influence VP at 2 and Alliance VP as a human does, but does not receive the resource bonus for reaching 4 Influence. A numbered Hagal Influence icon refers to that numbered position in the Rival card's Faction priority list.
answers.evidence: Rival Resources: Rival gains/loses Influence VP and Alliances but no resource bonus; Rival Combat says least Influence, leftmost tie; Agent turns explains numbered icon.

answers.answer: No. On a two-destination card, use only the destination selected by its condition; if occupied, reveal a new card rather than use the other destination. Accept Contract/Shipping are selected by Guild Influence, while Deliver Supplies/Heighliner are selected by Conflict tier.
answers.evidence: Rival Agent turns specifies the paired destinations and selection conditions; occupied chosen destination means reveal new card.

answers.answer: Yes. At every Rival Combat space, deploy up to two available garrison troops even if the card recruited none. Troops recruited at a noncombat space go to its garrison. A conditional bonus that requires 2+ Influence does not prevent Agent placement if unmet; simply apply only applicable Hagal effects.
answers.evidence: Rival Agent turns: Combat space deploy up to two from garrison even with no recruits; noncombat recruits garrisoned; lack of 2+ bonus never prevents placement.

answers.answer: Unless a post type is specified, the Rival uses the first available Faction observation post in priority order; if all four are occupied, ignore placement. Placing its third and final supply Spy immediately recalls its other two Spies and triggers its Scheme. Rivals never recall Spies for Infiltrate or Gather Intelligence.
answers.evidence: Rival Spies and Schemes section states all three rules.

answers.answer: If the Rival's Scheme recruits troops before its Agent placement and it then visits a Combat space that turn, deploy those troops too. A Place Spy card does not send an Agent; even when no legal post exists, ignore placement, immediately reveal another Hagal card and continue the turn.
answers.evidence: Rival Spies and Schemes; Rival Agent turns Place Spy procedure.

answers.answer: The Rival always collects accumulated bonus spice at a visited Maker space. At Hagga Basin or Deep Desert, if it has Hooks and the Conflict permits worms, summon one or two worms respectively instead of base spice. Without Hooks, or if it cannot summon due to Shield Wall protection, it takes the base spice instead (2 at Hagga, 4 at Deep Desert). The summary does not grant a choice to take base spice when Hooks and a worm-permitting Conflict allow a summon; in all cases it collects bonus spice. Imperial Basin always gives 1 base spice.
answers.evidence: Rival Maker spaces: always collects bonus; with Hooks and permitted Conflict summons; if none summoned takes base amounts; Imperial Basin always 1.

answers.answer: At the beginning of Combat, if the Rival has at least one unit deployed, reveal one Hagal card in turn order and add only its bottom swords to strength; if Reshuffle appears, reshuffle and reveal again. The Rival's strength is thus added before humans' normal Combat Intrigue window, so humans may respond afterward. A Rival with no unit deployed does not receive this bonus.
answers.evidence: Rival Combat: beginning of Combat, only if at least one unit, reveal card/add swords; Reshuffle repeats; humans then have normal Intrigue window.

answers.answer: Yes. The Rival gains control bonuses, defensive troops, battle-icon VP and ordinary sandworm reward doubling. It always takes optional Conflict VP if it can pay or recall required Spies. It never takes contracts: a contract reward gives it 2 Solari even with CHOAM.
answers.evidence: Rival Combat section explicitly covers control, defense, battle icons, reward doubling, optional VP and contract fallback.

answers.answer: During Resolve Reveal Effects, total and announce Combat strength and set the Combat marker at any point while resolving; update it as needed during the Reveal turn. Strength over 20 is marked by flipping to the +20 side and starting again from the beginning of the track.
answers.evidence: Reveal turn timing and Strength section: set at any point while resolving, update as needed; over 20 use +20 side.

answers.answer: A Leader's Signet Ring ability activates when you play Signet Ring on one of your Agent turns, not merely when you reveal the card. Card text may override the usual game rules.
answers.evidence: Setup 3 Leader abilities; Overview: “Cards of any type can override the usual rules of the game.”

answers.answer: A Recall Spy icon returns one of your Spies from an observation post to your supply, usually as a cost for an effect. By itself it is not automatically Infiltrate or Gather Intelligence; those are separate effects available when recalling without a card under their stated conditions.
answers.evidence: Special Rules — Spies defines Recall Spy icon and separately defines the two no-card recall choices.

answers.answer: The trash-an-Intrigue icon trashes one Intrigue of your choice from your hand. An ordinary discard instruction discards a card of your choice from your hand, but cannot be an Intrigue unless specified; discard is not trash.
answers.evidence: Trashing: separate trash-an-Intrigue icon; Discarding rule for ordinary discard.

answers.answer: Yes. Sandworm reward doubling lets you pay the reward's cost a second time for a second gain; if each gain is one freely chosen Influence, the two may be with the same Faction or two different Factions. By contrast, a single effect/icon that grants two freely chosen Influence requires both gains to go to one Faction.
answers.evidence: Sandworm reward doubling example permits 2 Influence with same or two different Factions; Influence section says one gain-two icon cannot split.

answers.answer: The Rival resolves the Signet Ring/Scheme ability printed on its Rival card. It is part of the revealed Hagal effect and does not require a human Signet Ring card or any Reveal turn; the Rival never Reveals.
answers.evidence: Rival Agent turns: apply revealed Hagal effects including Signet Ring; Rival never takes a Reveal turn; follows printed Signet Ring and Scheme abilities.

answers.answer: A Maker Hooks icon gives the Rival a Hooks token only if it lacks one; if it already has Hooks, it takes none. A Shield Wall removal icon removes the Wall only if the Rival has Hooks and the Wall remains. Without Hooks, ignore it; if the Wall is already gone, it has no further effect.
answers.evidence: Rival Hooks and Wall icons table specifies each state and result.

answers.answer: Secrets uses Bene Gesserit access, has no entry cost and is not a Combat space. It gives 1 Bene Gesserit Influence and draws one Intrigue from the Intrigue Deck; additionally, each opponent with at least four Intrigues gives you one selected at random.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide Secrets row and Steal Intrigue rule.

answers.answer: Imperial Basin uses Spice Trade access, costs nothing and is a Combat space. The visitor gains 1 base spice plus all bonus spice there. Its controller gains 1 spice; if the visitor is also controller, that same player receives both visitor and controller gains.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide Imperial Basin row; controlled locations rule resolves visitor effects and controller bonus even for same player.

answers.answer: Reveal the new Conflict from the top of the Conflict Deck and place it face up next to the deck, on top of any unclaimed Conflict cards from earlier rounds. Resolve any defensive troop bonus, then each player draws five cards from their own deck.
answers.evidence: Round Start phase: new card face up next to deck on top of prior cards; defensive bonus, then draw five.

answers.answer: Each human places one cube on the bottom space of each of the four Faction Influence tracks. Place Alliance tokens on the marked areas of all four tracks; no human begins holding an Alliance. The Shield Wall token starts on the marked area below Spice Refinery, so it is present initially.
answers.evidence: Setup 1 places Shield Wall and Alliance tokens on tracks; Setup 6 places one cube at bottom of each Faction track.

answers.answer: In 3–4 player play, the player with the First Player marker takes the first turn and play continues clockwise, one turn at a time; a player who Reveals is skipped for the rest of the phase. Player Turns ends when all players have Revealed. In Combat Intrigue, First Player has priority and play continues clockwise. Eligible players may play any number of Combat Intrigues or pass; a pass does not prevent acting later, and Combat resolves after all involved players pass consecutively.
answers.evidence: Player Turns and Combat sections specify clockwise order, Reveal skip/end, Combat priority and repeated passing rules.

answers.answer: The three Reveal steps are: (1) reveal all remaining hand cards face up, separate from Agent-played cards; (2) resolve Reveal-box effects of those newly revealed cards in any order, using Persuasion as desired and setting Combat strength during this step; (3) Clean Up all cards in front of you into your discard pile. Reveal effects need not follow card order.
answers.evidence: Reveal Turn steps list Reveal Cards, Resolve Reveal Effects “in any order,” then Clean Up.

answers.answer: Shuffle each human's ten-card starting deck and place it face down in their supply left of the Leader. Without CHOAM, omit CHOAM-marked cards; shuffle Intrigue and Imperium decks separately, face down, and deal five face up from Imperium to form the Row. Place Prepare the Way and The Spice Must Flow in separate Reserve stacks. The human Combat marker starts at 0; three Spies, Councilor and Control markers start in the player's supply; the four Influence cubes start at the bottom of their tracks.
answers.evidence: Setup steps 4 and 6 plus Initial card states table specify decks/Row/Reserve and component starts.

answers.answer: During a Reveal turn, ordinary Persuasion purchases are from any of the five Imperium Row cards or from Prepare the Way or The Spice Must Flow in the Reserve. Each cost is shown at the card's top right. Acquisitions may be made before, between or after Reveal effects, during that Reveal turn.
answers.evidence: Acquiring Cards section: Reveal turn; Row or Reserve; top-right cost; timing around Reveal effects.

answers.answer: Yes. Ordinary Spy placement and Recall Spy icons are optional even when a legal placement or recall exists. The Shield Wall detonation/removal icon lets you remove the token, so destruction is optional; once removed, it is gone for the rest of the game and cannot return.
answers.evidence: Special Rules — Spies says ordinary placement and Recall are optional; Shield Wall says when icon appears you may remove; cannot return.

answers.answer: Normally the played card needs an Agent icon matching the destination's upper-left icon, and the Agent sent comes from your Leader. A Spy connected to Shipping does not give a City-only card access to Shipping; a connected Spy alone does not grant all cards Spy access. If the card has the Spy Agent icon, it can send an Agent to a space connected to an observation post where you have a Spy, without recalling that Spy.
answers.evidence: Agent Turn and Spy rules: matching icon required; connected Spy alone insufficient; Spy Agent icon grants connected-space access.

answers.answer: Yes. During your Agent turn, you may first play a legal Plot Intrigue before placing your Agent; resources it grants before entry are available to pay the cost. Resources granted by the card used to send the Agent or by the destination are gained only after placement/effects, so they cannot pay for that entry.
answers.evidence: Player Turns explicitly distinguishes pre-placement Plot gains from after-placement destination/card effects.

answers.answer: No. Even after both humans have Revealed, continue the Rival's Agent turns while it has an Agent in supply. Combat begins only when both humans have Revealed and the Rival has used all its Agents. The Rival never takes a Reveal turn.
answers.evidence: Player Turns two-player rule gives exact end condition and says Rival never Reveals.

answers.answer: When the Conflict is revealed at Round Start, if you already control the location on that card, you may immediately deploy one troop from your supply directly to the Conflict without an Agent visit. After rewards, all Combat markers reset to 0 before the Makers phase.
answers.evidence: Round Start defensive troop bonus; Critical Locations & Control; Combat cleanup resets all markers to 0.

answers.answer: On an Agent turn, play one card from your hand face up in front of you and send one Agent from your Leader to a legal unoccupied space. Resolve its Agent box and the destination effects; ignore its Reveal box. You cannot reuse a card already in play or in your discard pile, or simply move an Agent already on the board; the rules direct playing a hand card and sending an Agent from your Leader.
answers.evidence: Agent Turn specifies card from hand and Agent from Leader, then Agent box; card anatomy says Agent box on Agent turn.

answers.answer: The restriction applies immediately when Shaddam plays Signet Ring to send the Agent; he cannot delay it by resolving board-space effects first. The restriction applies for that entire turn, so he cannot deploy units that turn.
answers.evidence: Shaddam's Signet benefits and FAQ Shaddam: restriction immediate, for that turn.

answers.answer: With four different positive strengths, first, second and third place receive their corresponding printed rewards; fourth place receives no reward. The highest-strength player wins and takes the Conflict card face up into their supply, then checks for a battle-icon match.
answers.evidence: Resolve Combat: four players can pay first/second/third; winner takes first and card; ordinary fourth gets none.

answers.answer: Players may choose a Leader or select one at random; Leaders do not have to be distributed randomly.
answers.evidence: Setup 3: each player takes a Leader “choose, or select at random.”

answers.answer: An ordinary draw-a-card effect draws from your own deck, reshuffling your discard pile into a new deck if needed. You may not choose a card directly from your discard pile. The Intrigue draw icon is separate and draws from the Intrigue Deck.
answers.evidence: Drawing cards special rule: ordinary draw from own deck, reshuffle if empty; separate Intrigue draw icon.

answers.answer: Shuffle the House Hagal deck and place it near the shared Rival, retaining the 2P Reshuffle card in the deck.
answers.evidence: Rival Setup: shuffle House Hagal and place deck near Rival, “retaining the 2P Reshuffle card.”

answers.answer: All four Maker Hooks tokens begin in the common bank; normal setup assigns none to a human. A token later acquired by a player moves from the bank onto that player's garrison.
answers.evidence: Setup 7: all four tokens in common bank; later acquired token moves onto player's garrison.

answers.answer: Yes. If a Combat Intrigue changes deployed units or otherwise changes strength, adjust the participant's Combat marker when that card resolves during the Combat Intrigue window. The Reveal-turn total is not fixed; use the adjusted strength shown on the track to resolve Combat.
answers.evidence: Combat phase: adjust marker when Intrigue resolves; Reveal total not fixed; resolve using adjusted track strength.

answers.answer: Gained Solari, spice and water come from the bank, and payments are returned to the bank. The summary does not direct taking resource tokens from another player's supply.
answers.evidence: Setup 7: whenever you gain resources, take from bank; whenever you pay, return to bank.

answers.answer: Shuffle all 20 standard contract tokens face down, then flip two face up as offers and leave the other 18 face down in the bank. Players do not choose offers or preset the order; the summary specifies shuffling before the two are exposed.
answers.evidence: CHOAM setup: “shuffle all 20: two offers and 18 in the bank.”

answers.answer: Before the contract shuffle, set aside both Sardaukar contracts under Shaddam's printed ability. Only Shaddam may acquire them, and setting them aside does not put them in his possession. Shuffle the remaining 18, reveal two as public offers and leave 16 face down in the bank, with the two reserved contracts separately set aside.
answers.evidence: CHOAM setup with Shaddam: set aside two before shuffle; shuffle 18, two offers and 16 bank; reserved contracts do not begin in his possession and only he may acquire them.
